## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md §4 (Health/HealthKit), keeping strictly within scope:

**Native bridge** (`ios/SparklingGo/SparklingGo/MethodServices/`):
- `HealthKitManager.swift` — wraps `HKHealthStore`, maps step-count sharing authorization to `notRequested`/`granted`/`denied`, requests read+write access, saves a 500-step sample (start=end=now), and queries 7 days of daily cumulative step sums.
- `HealthMethods.swift` — four `PipeMethod` subclasses (`health.getStatus`, `health.requestAccess`, `health.logSteps`, `health.getLastSevenDays`), auto-registered by Sparkling's `MethodRegistry.autoRegisterGlobalMethods()` since they subclass `PipeMethod` directly.

**Entitlements/Info.plist**: added `SparklingGo.entitlements` (HealthKit capability) and wired `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS`, plus `NSHealthShareUsageDescription`/`NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription` in the project's build settings (Debug+Release).

**JS side**: `src/pages/health/App.vue` now calls the native methods via `sparkling-method`'s `LynxPipe` (added as an explicit dependency), driving the status line, enabling/disabling the log button, and rendering the 7-day list per the exact label formats in the spec — with manual thousands-separator and weekday/month formatting rather than `Intl`, to avoid relying on PrimJS locale support. Native error text always surfaces on the status line.

Verified with `npm run build && xcodebuild ... build` — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, and confirmed the new Swift symbols and method-name strings are present in the compiled binary.

Note: I couldn't verify end-to-end HealthKit permission/data behavior in a running Simulator session (no UI interaction was performed this turn) — only that the build compiles and links correctly.
